en: Nor her glory, nor her freedom!
Still upon us, brothers, brave lads,
We too, brothers, shall be masters
Soul and body we shall lay down
And we shall show that we, brothers,
Come, let us set to the work!
Hey, hey, it is time to rise,
Call us from beyond the graves
Let us remember the glorious death
So that we do not lose in vain
Why did you give Ukraine away
We shall lay down our heads,
No one shall live to see us
notes: Romanization: the letters as printed in 1863 (і where modern spelling has ї, final ъ written ʺ, ь written ʹ, х written x).
line 1.2: literally 'And glory, and freedom!': neither the glory nor the freedom of Ukraine has died.
line 1.3: 'браття-молодці' is 'brothers, fine young fellows', a usual address in Cossack songs.
line 1.7: 'запануємо' is 'we shall rule, be our own masters'.
line 4.1-4.2: Severyn Nalyvaiko (d. 1597), Maksym Zalizniak (18th century) and Taras Fedorovych, called Triasylo (17th century), led Cossack and peasant risings.
line 4.6: 'Лицарства-козацтва', literally 'of the knighthood, of the Cossackdom'.
line 5.1: Bohdan Khmelnytsky, hetman, who in 1654 placed the Hetmanate under the Tsar of Muscovy.
line 5.4: 'москалі' is a disparaging name for Russians (Muscovites); 'погані' means bad, vile, also heathen.
